summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with a history of end-stage renal disease, diastolic heart failure, and diabetes was admitted for acute shortness of breath that began suddenly while watching television. She presented with hypertensive urgency and signs of pulmonary edema. EMS initiated CPAP and nitroglycerin, which improved her symptoms. In the hospital, she was managed with oxygen support, antihypertensives, and scheduled hemodialysis, which led to significant improvement in her respiratory status and fluid balance. A urine culture from a prior admission grew Klebsiella, prompting a short course of oral antibiotics. She was discharged home with nursing services, new instructions for a Sunday dose of Imdur to prevent interdialytic fluid overload, and education on medication adherence, fluid restriction, and infection monitoring.
